subject: Edge processing handoffs and subprocessor inventory — prospect Q&A

Subject: Quick Q: where do requests actually run (regions/subprocessors)?

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — great conversation. Before we move to procurement, our InfoSec team needs a concise picture of where customer requests execute across Redwood's surface: specifically (1) which regions handle inference for US/EU customers, (2) any transient "edge" handoffs (e.g., regional egress to a different cloud region), and (3) the list of subprocessors that may process or store payloads (KV cache, logs, observability traces).

Can you point us to a short, authoritative summary plus any inventory we can include in our security review? If there are different behaviors for Hosted API vs Dedicated/Private deployments, please call those out.

Appreciate it — we hope to close this month.

— Lena
Lena Horowitz
Head of Platform Security, VitaPulse Labs
security@vitapulse.ai

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Lena Horowitz <lena@vitapulse.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where do requests actually run (regions/subprocessors)?

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers below; attaching a one-page processing map and a CSV inventory for your reviewers. Short summary first, then a few specifics.

Summary (hosted API):
- Primary execution happens in the cloud region closest to the caller (US-West, US-East, EU-West, APAC regions we support).
- For latency optimization we operate ephemeral edge relay nodes in regions where we have presence; these relays forward requests to the designated execution region. Relays do not persist full payloads—only short-lived routing metadata and encrypted KV cache shards when beneficial.
- Subprocessors: cloud providers (region-specific), managed observability (trace aggregation), CDN provider for static assets, and a limited set of managed cache providers. Full CSV attached.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (differences):
- Hosted API: routing is policy-driven (region/latency/cost). Cross-border flows can occur if caller region is not identical to pinned model backbone; customers can pin region for stricter residency.
- Dedicated: reserved pools run in customer-isolated tenant clusters; you can choose region(s) and restrict egress—no cross-region fallback by default.
- Private: deployed into your VPC or on-prem; Redwood control plane can be configured to never route payloads outside your network.

Evidence we can provide: SOC 2 snapshots, subprocessor contracts, and a per-account processing map (we generated the attached PDF for VitaPulse). The CSV lists subprocessors and processing role (cache, logs, metrics, compute).

Next steps: if InfoSec needs, we can provide network diagrams with egress IPs and a short statement for procurement asserting no persistent storage of input payloads in relays (only ephemeral cache TTLs).

I'll follow up internally for any region-specific legal artifacts.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Hi Lena — following up with the more detailed answers your InfoSec asked for. I've expanded the earlier points and attached the CSV with the subprocessor roles flagged by geography. Key points for your memo: 

1) Cache & ephemeral data:
- KV cache: TTLs default to 5 minutes for inference prefix cache and 24 hours for session-level metadata; both are configurable per-account.
- Cache shards used for warm start optimizations may be stored in regional object stores or regional managed cache services. For EU-only residency, shards can be pinned to EU regions for Dedicated/Private customers.
- All cache layers are AES-256 encrypted at rest; keys are managed via our KMS. For Private/Dedicated you may supply a CMK (customer-managed key/HSM).

2) Edge relays & handoffs:
- Edge relays act as short-lived TCP/TLS proxies; they hold only routing headers and encrypted references to cache objects. No full request bodies are persisted beyond the TTL.
- In Hosted mode, the default routing policy favors the nearest execution region; cross-border routing can occur when a model variant is only available in another region. We include this behavior in the per-account processing map.

3) Subprocessors (high-level):
- Compute: Major public cloud providers (region-specific).
- Cache: Managed cache provider A (EU+US), Managed cache provider B (APAC-only).
- Observability: Traces aggregated by Redwood's managed observability partner (global, retention as per contract).
- Security: SOC 2 auditor and a narrow set of contract-managed partners. See attached CSV for full names and contactability.

4) Hosted mitigations and controls:
- If residency is a blocker, recommend Dedicated in a single region (we can commit to no cross-region fallback) or Private deployment in your VPC.
- We can add contractual controls: Data Processing Addendum clauses, Subprocessor list with 30-day notice, and attested encryption/HSM controls.

Attachments (sent): redwood-processing-map-2026.pdf (processing map, region pins), subprocessor-inventory-2026.csv (inventory with geography flag). Also linked: VitaPulse shared Drive doc with the map and our SOC 2 excerpt.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your InfoSec to walk the artifacts; propose Fri 14 May 09:00-10:00 PT.

Cheers,
